content_voiceover: This is the NCCN suggested treatment regimen table for follicular lymphoma, organized by line of therapy. First-line therapy for high tumor burden includes bendamustine, CHOP, or CVP combined with obinutuzumab or rituximab, plus lenalidomide-rituximab as an alternative. For low tumor burden, single-agent rituximab is preferred. Optional first-line extended therapy, meaning maintenance, includes rituximab every eight to twelve weeks for two years after chemoimmunotherapy, or obinutuzumab maintenance. For older or infirm patients unable to tolerate combination therapy, single-agent rituximab is preferred. Second-line therapy largely mirrors first-line chemoimmunotherapy options, but now also includes the novel combinations we just discussed, lenalidomide-rituximab plus epcoritamab, or lenalidomide-rituximab plus tafasitamab, both category one recommendations. Other second-line options include single-agent lenalidomide, obinutuzumab, or rituximab. Second-line extended therapy again offers rituximab or obinutuzumab maintenance. Third-line and subsequent therapy opens up to T-cell mediated approaches, including bispecific antibodies like epcoritamab or mosunetuzumab, and CAR T-cell therapies such as axicabtagene ciloleucel, lisocabtagene maraleucel, or tisagenlecleucel. Allogeneic transplant is reserved for select cases as third-line consolidation. This table is a dense but high-yield reference for how the treatment paradigm progresses from chemoimmunotherapy backbones toward increasingly targeted and cellular therapies with each relapse.
keypoints: First line: chemo plus obinutuzumab or rituximab for high tumor burden
Low tumor burden: single-agent rituximab preferred
Second line adds novel combos, len-R plus epcoritamab or tafasitamab
Third line: bispecifics, CAR T-cell therapy, or allogeneic transplant
